```{python}
#| include: false
# Shared setup for the figures that compare the pipeline against malariasimulation. The data is
# exported by misc/export_truth.py, which reads the simulation database directly. It is not
# regenerated at render time.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

plt.style.use("styles/mint.mplstyle")

TRUTH = "#f5f5f7"       # malariasimulation, averaged over its stochastic runs
PIPELINE = "#e66767"    # measured prevalence -> estiMINT -> stateMINT
EMULATOR = "#199e70"    # stateMINT given the simulator's own EIR
RUNS = "#8b93a3"        # the individual stochastic runs

truth = pd.read_csv("data/truth/edge_cases.csv")
truth_meta = pd.read_csv("data/truth/edge_cases_meta.csv")


def truth_panel(ax, case_id, predictor="prevalence", emulator=True, runs=True):
    """Draw one held-out parameter set: the simulator, the pipeline, and the emulator."""
    d = truth[(truth.case_id == case_id) & (truth.predictor == predictor)]

    if runs:
        for _, g in d[d.series == "run"].groupby("run_id"):
            ax.plot(g.years_from_campaign, g.value, color=RUNS, alpha=0.3, lw=0.7, zorder=1)

    # The simulator is drawn widest and underneath, so it reads as a band that the
    # predictions sit inside. Where a prediction leaves the band, the two disagree.
    layers = [("malariasim", TRUTH, 3.4, "-", 2), ("pipeline", PIPELINE, 1.8, "-", 4)]
    if emulator:
        layers.append(("emulator", EMULATOR, 1.5, (0, (4, 2.6)), 5))
    for series, colour, lw, ls, z in layers:
        g = d[d.series == series]
        ax.plot(g.years_from_campaign, g.value, color=colour, lw=lw, ls=ls, zorder=z)

    ax.axvline(0, color=RUNS, ls="--", lw=0.9, alpha=0.7, zorder=2)
    return ax


def truth_title(case_id):
    row = truth_meta[truth_meta.case_id == case_id].iloc[0]
    return row.description.replace(" - ", ", ")
```
